title: JavaScript DOM Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this JavaScript DOM course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does #title choose?
options: The element with id title
Every element named title
questions.explanation: The DOM gives JavaScript a way to work with the parts of a page. querySelector finds the first element that matches a CSS selector.

questions.question: What does textContent set?
options: A CSS stylesheet
Plain text inside the element
questions.explanation: textContent replaces the text inside an element. It treats new content as words rather than reading it as HTML markup.

questions.question: How many matching items does querySelectorAll choose?
options: All current matches
Only the first match
questions.explanation: querySelectorAll gives a list of all matches. You can use forEach to do a small job for every element in that list.

questions.question: What should classList.add receive?
options: The selector .bright with its dot
The class name bright without a dot
questions.explanation: classList changes class names on an element. CSS can then control what that class looks like.

questions.question: When does the listener run?
options: When the button receives a click
Only when the CSS file loads
questions.explanation: An event listener is a function that runs when an event happens. A click listener can change a page after a button is pressed.

questions.question: Where is the input's current typed text?
options: Its tag name
Its value property
questions.explanation: An input value is the text currently typed into a field. The submit event lets one handler work for a button click or the Enter key.

questions.question: Which step puts the new item on the page?
options: Appending it to the list
Only choosing its JavaScript variable name
questions.explanation: createElement makes a new page part. append puts that part inside an existing element.

questions.question: What does ?. protect against here?
options: The tip having a long sentence
Trying to remove a tip that is already gone
questions.explanation: The remove method takes an element out of the page. Other parts stay where they are.

questions.question: Where is this click listener attached?
options: The list parent
A separate listener on every book value
questions.explanation: Events often travel from a child to its parent. A parent listener can handle buttons that are added to a list later.

questions.question: What does input.focus() do?
options: Sends the input value to a server
Moves keyboard focus to the input
questions.explanation: Focus marks the control that receives keyboard input. The focus method can move the typing cursor to an input when that helps the reader.

questions.question: Why is Number used here?
options: To turn the stored text into a number
To count all elements on the page
questions.explanation: A data attribute stores a small extra value on an HTML element. JavaScript reads it through dataset as text.

questions.question: What happens to this count after a page reload?
options: It is automatically saved on another device
It starts at zero again
questions.explanation: A page can keep a number in JavaScript and show it in an element. Each click updates the number and then updates the displayed words.
